h: Tudor Halls, Shopping and the Ship Canal
p: Salford has more history than many visitors realise. Ordsall Hall, a short walk from the Quays, is a beautiful Tudor manor house with gardens and a reputation for ghost stories. It makes a fascinating contrast to the glass and steel of MediaCity.

Salford Museum and Art Gallery, near the university, has a recreated Victorian street, Lark Hill Place, which is a big hit with kids and adults alike. For football fans, Old Trafford, the home of Manchester United, is just a short walk across the Manchester Ship Canal.

If you need a spot of shopping, the Lowry Outlet at the Quays has a range of shops and places to eat, and the waterfront itself is lovely for a stroll, with views of the canal and the striking modern buildings around it.

On the trampoline front, the waiver form is the thing people forget, so get it done online at home. Pack drinks, dress in something stretchy, and expect the session to fly by; an hour of bouncing burns through energy faster than you'd think.
Parents can usually watch from the side, but joining in is half the fun. Just stretch first, because trampolining can be surprisingly hard work.

If you've got younger children, keep an eye out for toddler-focused sessions, which tend to be calmer and less busy. Older kids and teens might prefer the more active features, so check what's on at this branch before you book.
The Metrolink stop at MediaCityUK makes it easy to get here without a car.
